summary: First-contact record written by Mandel from a read-only reading of the session transcript and repository on 2026-10-20; the adversarial re-check of the headline numbers did not run (session limit), so every figure is the child's own and unverified. Child "Code optimization from chats" (session_015zuAYT7U87kT1nVYwows2L; pointlessbassmusic-byte/pointless-repo, branch claude/optimize-chats-to-code-qvrxca at 2e78799, one commit ahead of main in PR #89) has built a consolidated sports prediction and execution stack (sportsbot/: walk-forward Elo/Markov models, Polymarket, Polymarket US and Kalshi clients, a fail-closed risk layer with a double live opt-in, a tape-verified paper venue, a touch-maker arm and a per-arm allocation gate) beside an independent engine suite (polymarket-edge, kalshi-engine, arb-scanner), a frozen shadow-mode certification engine (substrate/) and a paper crypto arbitrage desk, deployed as paper on a Linode box. It measures everything against the price it would have paid, in closing-line value with market-clustered bootstrap intervals, and reports 25 results in docs/EDGE_VERDICT_2026-09-23.md: its MLB and tennis models carry no information the price lacks (Kalshi MLB beta +0.065, t 0.20, n 873; tennis Brier 0.2589 vs market 0.2024); favourite-longshot, drift, big-move fades, cross-venue boxes, PredictIt, BTC 5-minute windows and wallet copying all lose their costs; seven candidate reference prices (NWS, sportsbook consensus, Polymarket for Kalshi, the CPI nowcast, Deribit, spot for Kalshi crypto hourlies, the index for Kalshi index hourlies) are measured non-members, with the Fed decision bucket at >= 0.90 within 7 days the only member (18 meetings, 0 losses, +2.1% to +3.4%; across 15 banks the rule loses -0.69% and the G10 subset's 57/0 is a post-hoc split awaiting a forward record that has 0 fires so far); in-play MLB and NFL prices move before any feed (half the move 6 s after the pitch, 10 s after the snap). Its one positive number is a resting order at the touch of slow pre-game team-sport books, +0.5 to +0.9c of CLV per fill (Polymarket +0.0070 [+0.0058, +0.0082] at 120 s on 182 MLB markets; Kalshi +0.80c [+0.70, +0.92] net of maker fee on 396 games), which it states is an upper bound under a front-of-queue fill rule: strict fills are ~0 and counting the queue in front on 16 NHL games turns it to -0.24 to -0.64 pt. It is unsure of the fill share a new $1 order would get (unmeasurable from any tape), of whether the G10 split and the Polymarket-follows-Kalshi lead-lag (pooled 90 s +0.082 +- 0.017 but unstable across sessions) hold forward, and of NBA, soccer and the Polymarket US order mechanics. No live money has been placed; a pre-registered $1-a-side, 200-fill / 30-day live fill-share test (docs/MAKER_TEST.md, config/maker_test.yaml shipped inert) waits on the operator for keys, funding and the SPORTSBOT_LIVE=1 switch.
learnings: In-house rating models (MLB Elo + starting pitcher; bootstrapped tennis Elo) carry no information Kalshi's or Polymarket's price lacks; the tennis model is worse than the base rate and its bets lose ~18% per bet. | evidence: Results 2, 5, 8, 9: beta +0.065 t 0.20 (n 873 Kalshi MLB); beta -0.95 t -1.76 (n 392 Polymarket MLB); tennis Brier 0.2589 vs market 0.2024 (n 1,561), ROI -0.18 to -0.24 per bet; blending the model in makes the market worse at every lead. Walk-forward ratings, real quotes at first-pitch-anchored leads, fees as the executor charges them.

Takers lose to makers on Polymarket MLB (population taker CLV -0.14 to -0.33 pt); a CLV-selected set of wallets is informed out of sample (+1.0 pt, t ~6.7) but copying them across the spread nets -0.7 pt; leaderboard (P&L-ranked) wallets carry nothing. | evidence: Result 14 (685 markets, 760,382 fills, 70/30 time split): top-20 CLV wallets own-price +0.0101 [+0.0073, +0.0132], copy net -0.0071 [-0.0098, -0.0047]; Result 18: delay 2/10/30 s all -0.69 to -0.71; Result 21a: leaderboard rank correlation +0.12, copy +0.0 +- 7.1 pt.

Resting at the touch of slow pre-game team-sport books (MLB, NHL, NFL, CFB; soccer promising) earns +0.5 to +0.9c of CLV per fill, but ONLY under a front-of-queue fill rule; under strict trade-through fills it is ~0, and once the queue in front is counted a new $1 order that joins fills ~22% of the time and loses -0.24 to -0.64 pt. | evidence: Result 15 (+0.0070 [+0.0058, +0.0082] at 120 s, 182 markets), Result 24 (Kalshi +0.80c [+0.70, +0.92] front vs +0.14c [-0.18, +0.47] strict), Result 15 addendum 3 queue-counted table (main join 22% / -0.64 +- 0.23; Kalshi join 22% / -0.24 +- 0.31; first-at-new-price breaks even, 29-41 occurrences in 16 games).

Polymarket's tennis order book follows Kalshi's in active sessions (closing ~a quarter of the gap in 90 s, half in 7 min) and Kalshi never follows Polymarket; it is not a taker trade (gap mean 0.6 pt vs ~1.9 pt cost) and the maker version is the best-evidenced live experiment. | evidence: Result 10 addenda: pooled 90 s Polymarket->Kalshi +0.082 +- 0.017 (t 4.9) over nine active half-hours; sample 6 +0.230 +- 0.038 (t 6.0); sample 11 -0.04 +- 0.08 (sign flip); mark-outs of hitting the lagging ask -1.9 to -2.2 pt at every horizon.

The only confirmed 'reference-price' edge is the Fed decision bucket at >= 0.90 within 7 days (18 meetings, 0 losses, +2.1% to +3.4% net of 1c), and seven other candidate references (NWS, sportsbook consensus, Polymarket-for-Kalshi, CPI nowcast, Deribit, Kalshi hourly crypto vs spot, Kalshi hourly indices vs the index) are measured non-members. Across 15 central banks the rule loses (-0.69%); the G10 subset holds (57 fires, 0 losses, +2.3%) but the split is post hoc. | evidence: Resolved-market study (t 7.3 on 18 meetings); Result 20 table (87 fires, 3 losses: Colombia Apr/Jul 2026, Israel Aug 2026; G10 loss-rate bound 5.3% vs ~2.4% breakeven); Results 7, 21d, 22 and docs/SPORTSBOOK_, VENUE_LEAD_LAG_, CPI_NOWCAST_, CRYPTO_DERIBIT_ studies.

In-play betting on an official score feed is closed for MLB and the NFL: the venue prices a run/touchdown before or while the feed stamps it, and a taker at any realistic feed delay loses after fees; only sub-10-second (stadium/near-zero-delay broadcast) information is paid. | evidence: Result 23 (873 plays: venue half-move 6 s after the pitch, feed stamp 14 s; taker at 0 s -0.16c [-0.53, +0.20], 30 s -0.36c [-0.67, -0.03]); Result 25 (254 plays: half-move by snap +10 s 50%, +20 s 90%; taker +20 s -0.32c [-0.66, -0.00], +60 s -0.85c [-1.23, -0.47]; the +10 s +2.53c cell is selected on the post-price).

The Kalshi weather market already contains the NWS forecast: the forecast beats climatology but adds nothing to the price (beta +0.036, CI spans zero), and a fixed blend is worse than the price alone. | evidence: Result 7 on 168 settled strike-band rows / 28 station-days, station-day clustered; triple null coin 0.2500 -> climatology 0.1828 -> market 0.0751 (sportsbot weather-score).

No arbitrage class survives fees in 2026: no dutch books within a venue, no Kalshi-Polymarket box in 156 paired games, PredictIt boxes all negative after its 10% + 5% fees, combinatorial boxes are 1-2c longshots or name collisions, and the $39.6M literature figure belongs to the zero-fee 2024-25 regime. | evidence: Results 11 and 13; arb-scanner suspect-match quarantine; cryptoarb day-one -10 / -22 / -49 bps.

Every tested strategy on Polymarket's 5-minute BTC Up/Down windows loses (DMI/ADX below a coin; spot fair value only looked profitable with a 60 s look-ahead; complete sets and mean reversion lose; maker paired ladders lose in all 60 cells because the unpaired leg is the loser by construction); the one profitable wallet behind the posts is a two-sided market maker, and the last-seconds capture is a queue race against bids already at 0.999. | evidence: Results 12 and 18 (2,016 windows; 0 of 701 unpaired legs won; minute-4 >= 0.97 prints net +0.005 +- 0.001).

Model-free price patterns do not pay: fading or following big pre-game moves both lose the costs; the favorite-longshot bias in sports is calibration within noise; the pre-game home drift (+0.5 pt) is real but below one round trip. | evidence: Results 3, 6, 8, 9, 21c (MLB follow -1.89 +- 0.09, fade -1.52 +- 0.10 CLV on 102 moves).

Kalshi's hourly ladders are not slow to their underlying: BTC/ETH books beat a spot lognormal at every horizon and the S&P/NDX books beat an index lognormal by t ~8 at 30 minutes; a thin crowd is not a slow one. | evidence: Result 21d (328 events each) and Result 22 (5,597 events, pre-registered, both halves and both indices agree; taker -3.64 +- 0.45 pt).

CLV against the venue close is the only metric with enough power at this scale (PnL from hundreds of bets is noise), and the go-live gate must be CLV-based; but CLV and realised return diverge on fast-resolving esports books, so CLV is not a value proxy everywhere. | evidence: Power table (2% ROI needs ~10,000 bets; +0.005 CLV needs 79 observations); Result 15 addendum 2 (LoL/CS2 CLV positive, realised -0.09 / -0.11 with intervals excluding zero).

The fresh-wallet long-shot fade was a lead that failed its pre-registered holdout; nothing is built on it. | evidence: Result 21b holdout: +4.6 +- 3.0 (t 1.5), 96% of P&L from five markets, per-market mean -2.43.

Substrate/Echo: a frozen shadow-trial protocol tests H1 'a presentiment channel exists at d ~0.2' against triple nulls with an anytime-valid e-process; nothing stakes money in shadow mode. | evidence: substrate/PROTOCOL_v1.md (frozen 2026-09-04, hash 47e3c098...); dashboards and ARV CLI exist; no certification (E >= 20) is reported anywhere in the repo; the weather arm it feeds is a conventional baseline that loses to the market.
